# google_redis_cluster_auth_token

Represents an Auth Token for a Token Auth User within a Google Cloud Redis Cluster.


To get more information about ClusterAuthToken, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/cluster/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.clusters)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/cluster/)

~> **Note:** When token-based authentication (`AUTH_MODE_TOKEN_AUTH`) is enabled on a cluster (for the `default` user) or when a `google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user` is created, an initial token (`version-1`) is automatically created by the API.

Each user can have at most 2 active tokens at a time and must have at least 1 active token (deleting the sole remaining token for a user is rejected by the API; to abandon the last remaining token from Terraform state without calling the delete API—for example before destroying the parent user or cluster—set `deletion_policy = "ABANDON"`).

To perform zero-downtime token rotation: declare two `google_redis_cluster_auth_token` resources (acquiring the existing `version-1` token with `token_id = "version-1"` on the first resource and creating `version-2` with the second resource), update client applications to use the new token, and then remove the old token resource from the Terraform configuration.

~> **Warning:** All arguments including the following potentially sensitive
values will be stored in the raw state as plain text: `token`.
[Read more about sensitive data in state](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/manage-sensitive-data).

## Example Usage - Redis Cluster Auth Token Basic


```hcl
resource "google_redis_cluster" "token-basic-cluster" {
  name                        = "token-basic-cluster"
  shard_count                 = 1
  region                      = "europe-west4"
  authorization_mode          = "AUTH_MODE_TOKEN_AUTH"
  deletion_protection_enabled = false
}

resource "google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user" "token-basic-user" {
  cluster                     = google_redis_cluster.token-basic-cluster.name
  user_id                     = "token-basic-user"
  region                      = "europe-west4"
}

resource "google_redis_cluster_auth_token" "token-basic" {
  cluster                     = google_redis_cluster.token-basic-cluster.name
  user_id                     = google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user.token-basic-user.user_id
  region                      = "europe-west4"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `cluster` -
  (Required)
  The name or resource ID of the Redis cluster.

* `user_id` -
  (Required)
  The unique ID (username) of the Token Auth User.


* `token_id` -
  (Optional)
  The ID of the auth token (for example, `version-1`), or its full resource name.
  If specified and an active token with this ID already exists for the user (such as the initial `version-1` token automatically created with the cluster or user), Terraform will acquire and manage the existing token instead of creating a new one.
  If omitted, a new token version will be created on the server.

* `region` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the region of the Redis cluster.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}/authTokens/{{token_id}}`

* `name` -
  The full resource name of the Auth Token.

* `token` -
  The generated auth token string.
  **Note**: This property is sensitive and will not be displayed in the plan.

* `create_time` -
  The creation time of the auth token.

* `state` -
  The current state of the Auth Token.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


ClusterAuthToken can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}/authTokens/{{token_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}`
* `{{region}}/{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}`
* `{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import ClusterAuthToken using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    tokenId = "<-optional value->"
    region = "<-optional value->"
    cluster = "<-required value->"
    userId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_redis_cluster_auth_token.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import ClusterAuthToken using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}/authTokens/{{token_id}}"
  to = google_redis_cluster_auth_token.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), ClusterAuthToken can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_redis_cluster_auth_token.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}/authTokens/{{token_id}}
$ terraform import google_redis_cluster_auth_token.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}
$ terraform import google_redis_cluster_auth_token.default {{region}}/{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}
$ terraform import google_redis_cluster_auth_token.default {{cluster}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}
```
